title: 5. IP
content: #### Internetworking An arbitrary collection of networks interconnected to provide some sort of host-host to packet delivery service. - IP is a tool that runs on all the nodes in a collection of networks that defines the infrastructure through which these nodes and networks can function as an internetwork. # Internet Protocol (IP) Layer 3 within the OSI model. IP has the following characteristics: 1. Connectionless 2. Unreliable 3. Best effort 4. Datagram A **datagram** is the basic unit of information passed across an internetwork using **IP**. ### Fragmentation **Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU)**: The largest size (in bytes) of a data packet or frame that can be sent across a network. **Fragmentation**: When a router receives a datagram that it wants to forward over the network such that $bytes(datagram) > MTU$ of the outgoing link(s). **Solution 1**: The router fragments the IP datagram into multiple, self-contained datagrams. These fragments are only reassembled at the destination host not intermediate routers. - To avoid fragmentation, use path MTU discovery to find the smallest MTU along the path. ## IP Datagram Forwarding The process a router uses to move an IP packet, also called an IP datagram, from one network interface to another so it can get closer to its destination. A router tries in order based on the network number of the destination: 1. Delivering packet to connected interface if network number matches 2. Delivering packet to NextHop if included in forwarding table 3. Deliver packet to default router otherwise ## Addresses Globally unique and hierarchical. ### IPv4 - 32 bits long 5 classes originally but these were too rigid. This rigidity led to an inefficient use of address space, and a shortage of addresses. The resolution was subnetting / CIDR. 1. Subnetting within an organization to subdivide the organization’s network ID. 2. CIDR is basically the same idea as subnetting ### Subnetting Allows the flow of network traffic between hosts to be segregated based on network configuration. By organizing hosts into logical groups, subnetting can improve network security and performance. - **Subnet Mask**: Same format as IP (4 bytes). Applying the subnet mask to an IP address splits the address into two parts: 1. An extended network address with contains bits for the subnet identifier 2. A host address ### Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) Addresses two scaling concerns in the Internet; 1. The growth of backbone routing table as more and more network numbers need to be stored in them 2. Exhaustion on the 32-bit address space 1. Caused because of address assignment efficiency. If a network needs 2 hosts, we would need a Class C address which has 256 addresses. **CIDR Prefix:** X/Y where X is the fixed part belonging to a singular network. X (the prefix) can be of any length (unlike the class-based IP system). - Routes route based on these prefixes rather than storing one route for every individual host. #### Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) - Map IP addresses into physical addresses using a table. Broadcast the request if a table miss. ## DNS: Domain Naming System DNS maintains a hierarchal, distributed database of names. Servers are arranged in a hierarchy where each domain has a root server. An application needing an IP address is a DNS client.
